clue.text: Brutus's ability Antony made no claim to

definitions.text: Brutus's ability Antony made no claim to

parts.words: Brutus's ability Antony made no claim to
parts.note: in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Mark Antony's funeral speech protests 'I am no orator, as Brutus is', disowning the persuasive gift of speech

explanation.surface: A remark about the rival skills of two Roman politicians in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Antony's disclaimer is itself a piece of false modesty: his speech goes on to sway the crowd far better than Brutus's.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of persuasive public speaking is exactly what Antony pretends Brutus has and he lacks.

clue.text: Principal occupation, caption making

parts.note: the head is the principal, as of a school
one's line is one's trade or occupation, as in 'line of work'

explanation.surface: A job title that serves as the heading for a news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A title printed above a newspaper story is a caption summarising it.

clue.text: The house may' be full of -them

definitions.text: The house may' be full of -them

parts.words: The house may' be full of -them
parts.note: 'house' reads like a home, but in a theatre the house is the auditorium, full of audience members

explanation.surface: A host fearing a home crammed with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre talk the house is the audience or auditorium, and a full house means a sell-out.
explanation.definitionFit: People attending plays fill the auditorium on a sold-out night.

clue.text: No tears in this occupation

parts.note: 'tears' reads as weeping but means rents, splits; and occupation means living in a property, so here no rent is paid

explanation.surface: A cheerful job that never brings anyone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: A tear (rhyming with 'bear') is a rent, so 'no tears' gives the idea of paying no rent while occupying a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Living somewhere without paying the landlord anything is occupying it at no charge.

clue.text: Just the girl to form a circle

indicators.note: the letters are reshaped to form a new word

explanation.surface: Children choosing the right girl to make a ring for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female first name, so any girl may be it.

clue.text: A tart's made 'up in layers

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the article, the word tart and the S of 's taken as written

explanation.surface: A pastry assembled in layers, like a millefeuille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' looks like 'assembled' but in a down clue signals reading upwards; the S of the 's is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Geological beds of rock laid one above another are layers.

clue.text: How this' fish makes the sound of a dog

definitions.text: How this' fish makes the sound of a dog

parts.words: How this' fish makes the sound of a dog
parts.note: put the word 'How' before the name of this fish and you get a dog's long mournful cry

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a fish that barks like a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How' is not a question word here: it is the start of the word, and this cod-like fish completes the dog's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: This long cod-like sea fish's name, joined after 'how', spells a dog's long wail.

clue.text: What the fishwife has left on her hands ?

definitions.text: What the fishwife has left on her hands ?

parts.words: What the fishwife has left on her hands ?
parts.note: 'left on her hands' means unsold stock, the fish she could not sell

explanation.surface: A question about the unsold catch a fish-seller is stuck with.
explanation.walkthrough: A fishwife is a woman selling fish; the unsold fish and the jewellery on her fingers share one spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsold oily silver sea fish are what a fish-seller is stuck with, and 'her rings' are worn on her fingers.

clue.text: Retrospection was fatal to her

parts.note: in Genesis, the wife of Abraham's nephew looked back at burning Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: A grim warning about a woman undone by dwelling on the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospection' usually means reflecting on the past; here it is taken literally as looking behind you.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical woman who glanced back at the doomed city died for that single backward look.

clue.text: In Paraguay, tea at the end of, the game

definitions.meaning: the South American herbal infusion brewed from yerba leaves and drunk from a gourd
in chess, the final move trapping the king, as in checkmate

explanation.surface: A traveller's note about taking tea in South America as a match finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the yerba infusion of Paraguay and the chess finish that wins the game.

clue.text: Player responsible for runs

parts.note: reads like a cricketer scoring runs, but means a stage performer who also manages a theatre company and its runs of plays

explanation.surface: A cricketer credited with scoring the team's runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' and 'runs' point to cricket; in the theatre a run is a series of performances of one production.
explanation.definitionFit: The old-style head of a touring company both acted in and organised the seasons of its productions.

clue.text: Bulls are after such a favourable recognition

definitions.text: Bulls are after such a favourable recognition

parts.words: Bulls are after such a favourable recognition
parts.note: stock-market bulls hope prices will rise, and a rise in value is a gain; the word also means grateful recognition

explanation.surface: Cattle pursuing a good reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Bulls are investors who buy expecting prices to rise; a rise in value shares its name with grateful recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an increase in market value and a warm acknowledgement of someone's worth.

clue.text: Jabberwocky-style writing

parts.note: in Through the Looking-Glass, Alice first sees the nonsense poem printed backwards and must hold it up to a looking-glass to read it

explanation.surface: A description of nonsense verse in the manner of Lewis Carroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabberwocky-style' suggests invented nonsense words, but the point is how the poem was printed in the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversed script that reads properly only when reflected is named after the reflecting glass.

clue.text: First-class, Harry !'

definitions.meaning: excellent, splendid, as in the northern English exclamation of approval
Harry ... was a famous English music-hall singer, so his surname completes the name

explanation.surface: Someone praising a friend called Harry as top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Champion (1865-1942) was a London music-hall star known for songs like 'Any Old Iron'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an informal adjective for excellent and the surname of the music-hall singer Harry.

clue.text: Measures of confederacy

definitions.meaning: old units of distance, each about three miles
alliances or unions of states or groups bound together

explanation.surface: A phrase from history about the steps taken by an alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both old distance units of about three miles and alliances of allied parties.

clue.text: To' put game in dressing is a bind for anybody

indicators.note: the word game is put inside the word for the dressing

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds
taken as written

explanation.surface: Complaining that stuffing game birds with a dressing is a chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bind' looks like 'a nuisance', but means something that binds, here within any body.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough band of tissue binding bones together at a joint is found in everybody.

clue.text: They are held to have protective properties

definitions.text: They are held to have protective properties

parts.words: They are held to have protective properties
parts.note: 'held to have' sounds like 'believed to have', as of charms, but these things are literally held up in battle for protection

explanation.surface: A remark about amulets or remedies believed to guard against harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held to' looks like 'thought to'; read literally, these are things gripped on the arm as defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrior's defensive plates are carried in the hand to ward off blows.

clue.text: Feelings running wild this year

indicators.note: the letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Emotions getting out of hand over the past twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: An outburst of wildly uncontrolled emotion is a state of overwrought feelings.

clue.text: Mild cure possible with this instrument

indicators.note: the letters can possibly be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Gentle healing that might be done with some device.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument struck with small hammers is the musical instrument meant.

clue.text: Lines that are barely noticeable !

parts.note: 'barely noticeable' reads as faint, but means noticeable while bare, as with naked runners; the word also means thin lines

explanation.surface: A remark about faint stripes that hardly show.
explanation.walkthrough: To streak is to run naked through a public place; the noun also means a thin line or stripe.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrow stripes and dashes of naked running share one word.

clue.text: Upright if dumb recipient of a confidence

definitions.meaning: a vertical post, such as one a gate hangs from
from the saying 'between you and me and the ...', the silent witness to a shared secret

explanation.surface: Praise for an honest person who keeps secrets without a word.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase 'between you and me and the gatepost' introduces a secret; the post is the mute third party.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a vertical support for a gate and the silent listener in an old saying about secrets.

clue.text: He indulges in 1 ac, or eighteen letters

definitions.text: He indulges in 1 ac, or eighteen letters

parts.words: He indulges in 1 ac, or eighteen letters
parts.note: 1 ac is 1 across, the art of persuasive speech; the person meant can be called in six letters or described in the eighteen letters of 'indulges in' plus that answer

explanation.surface: A coded description of someone given to grand speechmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' means 1 across; 'indulges in' plus that 8-letter answer is eighteen letters, a long way of saying this six-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: A public speaker is someone given to persuasive, often flowery speechmaking.

clue.text: But do bicyclists make light of them ?

definitions.text: But do bicyclists make light of them ?

parts.words: But do bicyclists make light of them ?
parts.note: 'make light of' means shrug off; read literally, thin strips of wood or paper are used to make a light, while for cyclists the word means falls

explanation.surface: A question about whether cyclists shrug off their crashes.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both falls from a bicycle and slivers of wood or twists of paper for lighting fires or pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumbles off a bike share their name with the tapers used to carry a flame.

clue.text: It's said to give a false impression

definitions.text: It's said to give a false impression

parts.words: It's said to give a false impression
parts.note: something said aloud, a remark or claim, that misleads the listener

explanation.surface: A warning that a rumour may mislead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' looks like a hedge, 'reportedly'; read literally, the thing is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaccurate statement is a spoken or written claim that misleads.

clue.text: Is it located in Kent?

indicators.note: the word it is placed inside the letters standing for Kent

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is to be found in the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, so it stands for SE; the whole clue also asks where a thing is, its location.
explanation.definitionFit: A location or place where something stands is the thing the clue asks about.

clue.text: She contributes to their material

indicators.note: contributes to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman helping to supply what a group needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Any girl's name can be clued by a pronoun for a woman, and this is a female first name.

clue.text: It may contain many jots of -information

definitions.text: It may contain many jots of -information

parts.words: It may contain many jots of -information
parts.note: 'jots' sounds like 'tiny amounts', but jotting is writing quick notes, so this holds jotted notes

explanation.surface: A remark about something holding a great deal of trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a jot of information' means none at all; here jots are things jotted down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad for jotting down memos holds many hurried written records.

clue.text: Any wrens mingled with the "big birds here?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: Small wrens mixing in among much larger birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding place where swans are kept is where those large waterbirds live.
